FEMM Lab model against Motor-CAD Lab

Equivalent within engineering accuracy. Over the 840 points of the Motor-CAD efficiency map, the refined FEMM model is within 0.28 efficiency points on average, shaft torque within 1.6 %, total loss within 2.7 %. Over the 254 grid points: 0.15 points and 1.0 %. The largest remaining difference is the hysteresis part of the iron loss (-15 %); eddy loss agrees within 4 %, and iron loss overall is -7 %, a small share of the total.

1. How the FEMM model was refined

The first FEMM Lab build (2D, full machine) matched the back-EMF but its torque at full current sat about 1 % under Motor-CAD, and adding the Motor-CAD rotor skew made that worse. The cause was traced to the q-axis flux, then fixed step by step:

Half-machine model
12 slots / 10 poles repeat every 180° with the sign flipped: the model is one half with anti-periodic boundaries and FEMM's air-gap element (fixed meshes, no remeshing per rotor position). Same results as the full machine within 0.1 % (flux linkage) and 0.2 % (torque), 2.2–2.8 × faster.
Stacking factor in the field solution
With the steel BH curve reduced by the 0.97 stacking factor, FEMM's q-axis flux was 3–8 % under Motor-CAD while the d axis matched. A one-at-a-time sensitivity study (table below) shows that only the stacking factor has that signature. Motor-CAD's flux map is reproduced with the BH curve applied unreduced (fill 1.0); 0.97 stays in the masses and the iron loss, which match Motor-CAD's masses exactly.
Rotor skew
Motor-CAD skews the rotor in 3 slices at −2 / 0 / +2° mechanical, and its Lab includes it (its d-axis flux at zero current, 19.835 mV·s, is the skewed open-circuit value). FEMM evaluates each slice with the stator current turned by ∓10° electrical in that slice's rotor frame, turns the flux back and averages: exact for the fundamental, and correct under saturation.
Torque
Motor-CAD Lab torque is 1.5 p (ψd iq − ψq id) (its 44.76 N·m at 1000 rpm reproduces exactly). The refined FEMM model uses the same expression; the FEMM air-gap force torque is shown as the 2D variant.
Iron-loss grid
Fixed-mesh, full-cycle field solutions (30 points per cycle, as Motor-CAD) at 4 d-axis × 5 q-axis currents (was 4 × 3), Motor-CAD's Steinmetz coefficients with the 2π² eddy convention and build factor 1.6. The finer grid showed that the first build's 3-level fit had over-predicted the loss at light load by 20–30 %, which happened to offset an under-prediction; on the true curve, the first-build formulation was 18 % low.
Iron-loss formulation
Motor-CAD's loss settings include a minor-loop factor Kc = 0.65 that the first build ignored. Hysteresis now uses the peak flux density per element and component with the Lavers minor-loop factor 1 + Kc·ΣΔBminor/Bpk; eddy loss uses the sum over harmonics (the dB/dt content). Both come from the same saved field solutions, with no new FEA and no fitted factors.

5. d-q flux linkage and torque at the same currents

6. Open circuit (from the back-EMF validation)

Back-EMF fundamental 10.35 V against Motor-CAD 10.36 V at 1000 rpm, Ke 0.0969 against 0.0980 V·s/rad, magnet flux 19.77 against 19.83 mV·s, THD 1.48 % against 1.25 %.

7. What still differs, and why

  • Hysteresis loss (-15 %, larger at high speed in field weakening). Eddy loss now agrees, so the field waveforms and frequencies are right; the remaining gap is in how the hysteresis loop is counted. Motor-CAD's exact minor-loop algorithm is not documented in the exported data. FEMM counts loops from 30 samples per cycle per flux component. A further candidate is the lamination fill: if Motor-CAD evaluates the loss at the steel flux density B/0.97, that alone adds about 6 % (0.97−2.07). It was not applied because it cannot be confirmed from the exports. Iron loss is 1–3 % of the input power, so efficiency stays within about 0.1 point.
  • Rotor iron loss (-13 %). In a spoke ferrite rotor it comes only from slot and MMF harmonics, the most method-dependent term; a few watts.
  • AC copper loss is a few watts; both use the hybrid method with adjustment factor 2, FEMM from its own slot field.
  • Current and phase advance at high speed: where the voltage limit is active, small flux differences move the MTPA point along the voltage ellipse; the shaft torque and efficiency stay close because the operating point is defined by them.

8. Method and files

FEMM model
backemf.py (geometry from the Design9795_1 screenshots; SYM=1 half model; STACK_FEA), lab_map.py (d-q flux map 6 × 6 currents × 4 rotor positions), iron_loss_age.py (iron loss), iron_fit.py (iron-loss formulations from the saved fields), lab_model.py (Lab: losses, limits, skew slices, torque; loss model v3), make_lab_v2.py (maps), compare9795.py (this comparison).
Motor-CAD
Map_1.xlsx, envelop_1.xlsx, Grid.xlsx (Lab, 100 °C), M235-35A.xlsx; same BH curve and loss coefficients in FEMM.
Settings
DC 52 V, modulation index 0.95, 360 A rms line, Idc 280 A, delta, 10 turns/coil, 2 parallel paths, SWG 11, MLT 203.6 mm, end-winding inductance 1.954 µH, bearing and windage loss as Motor-CAD (148.9 W at 9000 rpm).
